# Purpose

I lock scope here before the literature review, umbrella plan, and Ethix application. This note is one page of decisions and open points. It does not replace the protocol.

**Status:** Draft — awaiting sign-off by responsible researcher.

# Population and setting

- **Population:** Adults (≥18 years) who undergo planned surgery under anaesthesia.
- **Setting:** **Karolinska University Hospital** — perioperative and anaesthesia care. Mixed surgical categories (aligning with the ICD-10 groups in the Ethix draft).
- **Unit of analysis:** The surgical episode and linked preoperative assessment period, unless a sub-study states otherwise.
- **Inclusion (working):** Patients with sufficient chart and structured perioperative data for the planned analyses.
- **Exclusion (working):** Episodes with no usable preoperative record or missing outcome linkage.

**Open:** Final inclusion rules after data access is confirmed with the hospital.

# Data sources and access

| Source | Content | Role |
|--------|---------|------|
| Karolinska EHR (journal) | History, examination notes, assessments, comorbidity | Chart review; AI-assisted extraction in controlled environment |
| Structured perioperative data (Karolinska) | Anaesthesia records, surgery codes, timings, labs where available | Exposures, covariates, outcomes |
| Registers (as approved) | Outcomes, diagnoses, mortality, readmission | Validation and follow-up beyond index admission |

- **Access route (to confirm):** Research agreement with Karolinska Universitetssjukhuset / relevant data controller; register extracts via approved pathways where needed.
- **Ethix alignment:** Register and journal data (`§10.1`); sensitive health data; no direct participant contact in the current Ethix draft (`§9.1` Nej).

**Open:** Named supplementary registers, legal basis for each source, and data processor agreements.

# Design

| Track | Guideline | Status |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| **Primary:** Observational study at Karolinska | SPIROS | In scope for ethics application |
| **Contingent:** Trial of AI-supported vs usual pathway in care | SPIRIT 2025 | Not started; separate protocol and amendment if pursued |

This project has **two parallel workstreams**. Both use the same data boundary and AI rules below. They differ in question and evaluation method.

## Workstream A — Epidemiological associations

Standard observational research:

- Estimate associations between patient-level factors (demographics, comorbidity, functional status, investigation results, chart-derived signals) and perioperative outcomes.
- Retrospective and/or prospective cohort using routinely collected Karolinska data.
- No change to clinical care solely because of this workstream.

## Workstream B — Agentic anaesthesia planning (in-vitro)

Development and **in-vitro** evaluation of AI agents that draft:

1. **Pre-operative** anaesthesia and perioperative management plans from chart and structured data.
2. **Intra-operative** anaesthesia plans (where data and use case allow).

Evaluation is **off-line**: compare agent outputs to documentation, guidelines, and clinician review. No autonomous use in live care during this phase.

# Outcomes to explore

I will consider **multiple outcomes** without ranking them as primary or secondary at this stage. The literature review and data availability will guide which outcomes enter each analysis.

**Candidate outcome domains:**

- Major perioperative morbidity (domain-specific or **composite**)
- Critical care escalation (unplanned ICU/HDU or equivalent)
- Mortality (in-hospital and/or fixed horizon where follow-up exists)
- Length of stay and readmission
- Procedure-specific complications where counts allow

**Composite outcomes:** I will define composites explicitly when used (component events, window, handling of competing events). I will not pre-specify a single primary composite here.

**In-vitro evaluation metrics** (workstream B, not patient outcomes):

- Completeness and accuracy of chart extraction vs human reference (subset)
- Plan quality against guideline and documentation criteria
- Consistency and safety flags on agent-drafted pre-operative and intra-operative plans

Exact definitions, codes, and analysis hierarchy will be fixed in the statistical analysis plan after the literature review.

# AI processing boundary

- AI and agents are **assistive only**. A licensed clinician remains accountable for any clinical decision.
- Workstream B produces draft plans for research evaluation only. I will not deploy them in live care during this phase.
- Identifiable chart text stays in approved environments. External APIs (e.g. OpenRouter) only with explicit approval and contractual controls; prefer local open-weight models for identifiable data where feasible.
- I will log prompts, model versions, and outputs as allowed by ethics and the data controller.
- I will disclose AI-assisted writing and research methods (see `docs/ai-transparency.md` and the attribution ledger).
